title: Budapest or Krakow at Christmas?
author: Brogan
intro: Budapest and Krakow are two of the cheapest and most atmospheric Christmas market cities in Europe. Budapest has grand markets and hot thermal baths. Krakow has one of Europe's biggest medieval squares and a cosier feel. Here's how to choose.
seo_title: Budapest or Krakow at Christmas? Markets, costs (2026)
seo_description: Budapest for grand markets and thermal baths, Krakow for a cosy medieval square and lower prices. Market dates, weather and costs compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Choose [Budapest](/destinations/budapest)** for two big, polished markets, a grand river setting and the chance to sit in a steaming outdoor thermal bath in December.
- **Choose [Krakow](/destinations/krakow)** for a cosier, more traditional market in one huge medieval square, lower prices and a compact old town you can walk round in a day.

Both have cheap direct flights from many UK airports, and both work well for a long weekend.

sections.heading: The markets
sections.text:
**Budapest** has two main markets, and both were expected to open on **13 November 2026**:

- **Vörösmarty Square**, the oldest, with craft stalls, food and mulled wine. It usually runs until about the end of December, with the craft stalls closing a few days earlier.
- **St Stephen's Basilica**, with an ice rink around a Christmas tree and a light show projected on to the front of the basilica in the evenings. It usually runs into the first day of January.

**Krakow's** main market fills the Main Square (Rynek Główny), one of the largest medieval squares in Europe. When we checked, the 2026 dates hadn't been announced, but it usually runs from **late November to 1 January**. Expect wooden stalls selling grilled oscypek cheese, pierogi, sausages, mulled wine and handmade decorations, with St Mary's Basilica towering above.

In early December, Krakow also shows off its famous **szopki**: elaborate, glittering nativity scenes modelled on the city's churches. The tradition is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

Check official dates before you book, as both cities confirm them in the autumn.

sections.heading: What else there is to do
sections.text:
**Budapest:**

- **Thermal baths.** The outdoor pools at Széchenyi are open all year, and sitting in hot water as steam rises into the cold air is the highlight of a winter trip for many people.
- **The Danube.** Walk or take a short cruise past the Parliament building, which looks spectacular lit up at night.
- **Buda Castle and Fisherman's Bastion** for views over the river and the city.

**Krakow:**

- **Wawel Castle and Cathedral**, on a hill above the river.
- **Kazimierz**, the old Jewish quarter, now full of cafés and bars.
- **Wieliczka Salt Mine**, a short trip from the city, with chapels carved from salt deep underground.
- **Auschwitz-Birkenau**, about an hour and a half away. It's a sombre, important visit that takes most of a day, so plan it for a separate day from the markets.

sections.heading: Weather
sections.text:
Both are cold in December, and Krakow is usually a little colder:

- **Budapest:** daytime highs of around 3 to 5°C.
- **Krakow:** daytime highs of around 1 to 3°C, with frosty nights.

Snow is possible in both but not guaranteed. Pack a warm coat, a hat, gloves and shoes with a good grip, as cobbles get icy. If you want a better chance of snow, our guide to [where to go for a white Christmas](/blog/where-to-go-for-a-white-christmas) has colder options.

sections.heading: Cost
sections.text:
Both are good value compared with Western European Christmas markets like [Vienna](/destinations/vienna) or [Strasbourg](/destinations/strasbourg). Krakow is usually the cheaper of the two, especially for eating out and drinks.

Hungary uses the **forint** and Poland the **złoty**, so you'll need a card without foreign transaction fees, or some local cash for market stalls. Many stalls take cards, but not all.

Hotels in both cities go up in price on December weekends, so book early or go midweek.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
There are direct flights to both cities from London and many regional UK airports, taking about two and a half hours. Krakow's airport is about 20 minutes from the city by train, and Budapest's is about 30 to 40 minutes by bus or taxi.

Our guides to [where you can fly direct from Manchester](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-manchester-airport) and [from Stansted](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-stansted-airport) list the routes from those airports.

sections.heading: Which one should you choose?
sections.text:
**Pick Budapest if:**

- You want a grander city with big views and more to do at night.
- The idea of an outdoor thermal bath in winter appeals.
- You'd like two different markets in one trip.

**Pick Krakow if:**

- You want the most traditional, cosy market atmosphere.
- Lower prices matter.
- You like a small, walkable old town and don't mind the cold.

If you're comparing more cities, our posts on [Vienna or Prague at Christmas](/blog/vienna-or-prague-at-christmas) and the [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe) cover the others. Our [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page has more festive ideas.

Still can't agree? Add both to a shared list on somewhere.party, give them points, and let a draw decide. Our guide to [how to decide where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday) explains how.

faqs.question: When do the Budapest Christmas markets open in 2026?
faqs.answer: The main markets at Vörösmarty Square and St Stephen's Basilica were expected to open on 13 November 2026. Vörösmarty usually runs until around the end of December, and the Basilica market into 1 January.

faqs.question: When is the Krakow Christmas market in 2026?
faqs.answer: When we checked in October 2026, official dates hadn't been announced. The market usually runs on the Main Square from late November to 1 January.

faqs.question: Is Krakow cheaper than Budapest?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes, especially for food and drink. Both are much cheaper than Christmas markets in Austria, Germany or France.

faqs.question: Are the Budapest thermal baths open in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes. The outdoor pools at Széchenyi are open all year, and they're one of the best things to do in Budapest in December.
